ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brown with a distinct dark interorbital bar and a pale belly. Key features include a blunt snout and granular skin on the dorsum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Philautus microdiscus* is best distinguished by its distinct, prominent, and rounded adhesive discs on the fingertips, which are significantly larger than those of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Philautus microdiscus* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kobo Bubble-nest Frog is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects among the dense vegetation of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Philautus microdiscus* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in terrestrial foam nests. Development is direct, bypassing the tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Philautus microdiscus* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests and grasslands of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kobo Bubble-nest Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard while calling from vegetation near forest streams.
